newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to prod Italy, China on global rubber pact.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to prod Italy, China on global rubber pact.

text.p: Malaysia will prod Italy and China to lend their support to a new world rubber price pact which needs endorsement from just one more country to take effect, the national Bernama news agency reported on Thursday.

The International Natural Rubber Agreement 3 (INRA 3) should have come into force on January 1 and Malaysia's Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik is pursuing the matter with Italy and China, which have both verbally committed to the pact, Bernama said.
INRA 3 can come on board with ratification from 75 percent of the world's rubber consumers and producers.

Lim said the producers have fulfilled their voting rights quota but the consumers lacked 1.6 percent in support. He said he will meet the ambassadors of Italy and China soon to expedite their official support.

INRA 3, a United Nations-brokered pact, is the world's only remaining global commodity agreement with economic provisions and a buffer stock that allows the industry to buy and sell rubber to stabilise prices.

The agreement was held up previously by Indonesia and Malaysia -- two of the world's largest rubber producers who both wanted the top executive director's post in the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) for ratifying the pact.
INRO sources said this week that Malaysia's Primary Industries deputy secretary-general Ahmad Zubeir Noordin has been picked as the new executive director for INRO.
Lim did not confirm Ahmad Zubier's appointment but said he will fly to Indonesia "to personally thank the Indonesians" for ultimately supporting Malaysia for the executive director's post.
INRO, the administrator for the INRA 3, also said this week that Italy's two percent voting right was crucial to make up the consumer quota. But it added that China's participation was negligible.
